item.description:
Rein 0.8.12

  • Menu bar tidy now holds its arrangement — permanently. Two changes behind one fix:

- Rein now keeps its own record of where the ⋮ divider and ‹ chevron belong, and restores them there on every launch. (macOS's own position memory was being wiped by its quirks — the reason the divider kept "resetting" after a restart.)

- Rein now remembers *which* icons you tucked away. If one escapes back onto the visible bar — after a restart, a display wake, or an app re-creating its icon mid-session — Rein briefly reveals the hidden section, slides the stray back behind the divider, and tucks everything away again, automatically. This needs Accessibility access (already granted if you use Rein Remote's mouse control); without it, Rein tells you once in the Activity log and leaves things be.

Rein 0.8.11

  • Rein Remote reconnects reliably. A network blip could send the Mac's relay connection into a

silent churn loop — the iPhone app then searched for the Mac forever. The connection layer now

recovers from drops cleanly, and both apps detect a "zombie" link (connected in name only) within

seconds and rejoin on their own. After updating, open Rein's window, pick Remote in the sidebar,

and tap Redeploy once so your relay picks up the matching server-side fix.

  • Hidden menu bar icons stay hidden. Icons tucked behind the ⋮ divider could reappear after the

display slept, a monitor was plugged in, or the screen resolution changed — and on wider displays

the reveal chevron itself could vanish into the hidden section. The hidden section now re-asserts

itself after every such event, sizes itself to your actual displays, and self-repairs if macOS

shuffles the controls out of order.

Rein 0.8.10

  • A clearer tuck-away arrow. The menu bar tidy toggle now uses a bolder ‹ › arrowhead instead of the slim compact chevron, which read as a straight line next to the ⋮ divider.
